claim_summary: For every integer \(n\ge2\), radius \(\delta>0\), and real symmetric cubic tensor \(T\), consider central two-point finite-difference gradient estimation at zero on \(f(x)=T[x,x,x]/6+\phi(x)\), with \(\phi\) even and differentiable. For a Haar-uniform complete orthonormal frame and \(t_i=\sum_jT_{ijj}\), the estimator mean is \(\delta^2t/[2(n+2)]\), and its orientation variance is exactly \(\delta^4\|H\|_F^2/[6(n+2)(n+4)]\), where \(H_{ijk}=T_{ijk}-(t_i\delta_{jk}+t_j\delta_{ik}+t_k\delta_{ij})/(n+2)\). The orientation variance vanishes if and only if the cubic is radial-linear, i.e., \(H=0\). For unit rank-one \(T=a^{\otimes3}\), the Haar frame has lower squared gradient risk than the fixed coordinate frame if and only if \(\sum_i a_i^6>15/[(n+2)(n+4)]\), with equality at the boundary. This criterion holds unchanged with independent equal-variance additive noise at each function evaluation. Both strict orderings arise for every \(n\ge2\), including at the unique global minimizer of an explicit uniformly strongly convex quartic objective.
integrity: Proof uses spherical fourth/sixth moments and exact harmonic tensor orthogonality; finite rational tests are supplementary, not an independent audit.
scientific_limitations: Complete Haar real orthonormal frames and central two-point differences only.
Cubic odd part plus arbitrary even differentiable part; zero-gradient evaluation point.
Independent equal-variance additive measurement noise; not correlated noise or general optimization trajectories.
Unindexed equivalent harmonic-tensor specializations may exist.
title: Harmonic-cubic rigidity and a sharp localization crossover for orthogonal-frame finite differences
